errors.description: The key's hosted account is suspended, banned, or has not accepted the Trust Pledge.
Your AI provider rejected the key, or the key may not use this model.
Your AI provider refused the request, for example an unknown model.
The input is too large for the model's context window.
The AI profile's base URL is not allowed by the endpoint policy.
The model's answer was not the JSON that was asked for, even after one repair.
Your AI provider failed for a reason without a more specific AI failure code.
Your AI provider account cannot pay for the call.
Your AI provider rate-limited the call.
Your AI provider refused to answer (a content filter or safety refusal).
Your AI provider did not answer in time.
Your AI provider is unavailable: an outage or a connection failure.
The request was refused as it stands, for example a refused job or an invalid artifact file name.
This deployment cannot render pages in a browser; use the static engine.
The job's estimate is above the request's max_credits; nothing was reserved.
The request conflicts with one still in progress (the same Idempotency-Key) or with a job that has not finished.
A policy gate refused the job before it started, for example a crawl target that is not allowed.
The job needs a validated proxy and the caller has none; nothing was sent.
The job's proxy could not be used, so the page was not fetched.
An error without a more specific code.
The page could not be fetched: a network error, a timeout or an error response.
The key is valid but may not do this: a missing scope, a disabled endpoint or command, or a key not bound to a hosted account.
The account does not have the credits this job needs.
An MCP tool failed unexpectedly; the details are only in the server log.
An unexpected failure; retry once, and quote the request ID when reporting it.
The job stopped before it finished, for example on a service restart.
An artifact must be named by a single file name from the job's artifact list.
The request is malformed or outside a documented bound; field errors never echo the submitted values.
MCP over HTTP: the bearer key was not accepted.
The job did not finish within its time limit.
The key of an open listen stream was revoked; use an active key.
A listen stream reached its lifetime; listen again.
The route does not accept this HTTP method.
The resource does not exist or is not the caller's (the two are never distinguished), or there is no such route.
The request body is larger than the route accepts.
The destination policy refused the page before any fetch.
Too many requests for this account; wait Retry-After seconds, then retry.
A scrape's JSON step was interrupted; scrape the URL again, or extract from the job.
The job's charge could not be settled or confirmed; its failure_reason says whether anything was charged. Check it before sending the request again.
The first request with this Idempotency-Key failed after it may have started work; list your jobs, then retry with a new key.
MCP over HTTP: the key store is unavailable; retry after Retry-After seconds.
The caller already has the maximum number of running or queued jobs, or the browser renderer is busy; retry after Retry-After seconds.
The caller already holds the maximum number of open listen streams; close one first.
No credential was sent, or the API key or admin token was not accepted.
A feature or service the request needs is turned off or not running on this deployment.
The artifact name resolves outside its job's files.
The request body's content type is not accepted.

fields.code: The stable machine-readable code; match on it, never on the message.
fields.http_status: The HTTP status that carries the code on ApexAPI or MCP HTTP; null when it is only an MCP tool error or a failed result's error_code.
fields.retryable: Whether the same request can succeed if sent again later unchanged; honour Retry-After when the response has it.

surfaces.apexapi: An ApexAPI error response: the envelope {"error": {"code", "message", "request_id"}}, or {"detail", "code"} for authentication, scope, request-schema and route failures.
surfaces.mcp: An MCP error: a tool or resource error whose text starts with [code], a JSON-RPC error whose data.code is the code, or, over MCP HTTP, a {"error", "error_description"} body.
surfaces.result: The error_code of a failed scrape or asset result (the request itself succeeded). A failed result may also carry a request-error code met while the result was rendered.
